purpose: Every capability worker is either named by a transport route or listed here with a reason. Twice in this session a worker existed with no route pointing at it, which made a present capability look missing; this record is how that stays visible instead of recurring.

unrouted.reason: three independent reasons, of which the recorded one was only the third. (1) It returns no projected text: its result is a duration, an extracted 16 kHz mono audio path and a list of sampled keyframes with hashes - real measurements, but no text. The route contract is a projected text and the Core derives canonical line anchors from it and refuses a receipt whose structure does not match, so no parameters field would make this worker routable. (2) It produces file artifacts (the audio WAV and the JPEG frames) and the attempt directory is temporary, so routing it also needs an artifact-transfer shape the PDF and archive routes have but this one would need in a different form. (3) It takes an output directory and frame interval/cap options, and parameters are currently required to be empty. Routing frame extraction therefore needs an artifact-and-measurement contract alongside, or instead of, the text-projection contract - a deliberate design decision, not a flag. Unrouted on purpose and recorded here.
unrouted.what_it_would_serve: F11 (MP4/MOV/MKV/WebM): frame events, sampling coverage, and a 16 kHz mono audio track for the ASR lane

unrouted.reason: two reasons, and the first is what makes this entry unusual: the worker is **reachable**, just not through job dispatch. (1) It is served by the Core route `POST /api/v1/machine/answers`, which accepts a knowledge id and a question and runs this worker as a process through the same boundary every engine-calling capability uses. The job protocol cannot carry that route: a route in the transport table is validated with `parameters` required to be empty, so there is nowhere for the question to travel, and declaring one would be a route that fails its own validation. (2) Its result is an answer and a loss receipt rather than a projected text with canonical anchors, so the text-projection contract does not describe it either. Not a job route on purpose, reachable through an owned Core route, and recorded here so a reader can tell that from a missing capability.
unrouted.what_it_would_serve: G4 (machine co-learning lite): a grounded model answer over an accepted knowledge item, as a candidate for a human to find a real error in

also_present_but_not_capability_workers.note: takes a URL and an output directory and fetches the page; it is a fetch client, not an extraction capability, and no route may reach the network. F03 (dynamic and long pages) therefore has no fetch path at all: only a saved snapshot can be read, and pagination or scroll coverage cannot be recorded without a browser. It also returns no projected text, so it could not satisfy the route contract even if a network fetch were in scope - the same structural limit that keeps media/worker_video.py unrouted.
a dispatcher with no engine identity of its own; it selects another worker rather than producing a receipt.

routed_since_this_record.note: routed on 2026-10-01. The recorded reason for leaving it unrouted was that no model was configured anywhere the repository could see; that is resolved by resolving the model through the declared capability registry, with ARCHEAXIS_ASR_MODEL_DIR and a declared-path fallback, and it was verified end to end on a real Chinese recording through the real sidecar protocol: language zh at 0.9983, 2 segments over 8,940 ms, engine python-worker-transcribe 0.1.0, covered 2 of 2. Kept here as history because the exemption was real until the model resolution and the audio media types existed.

routed in round 84 after being listed here as unrouted. It is a model call (default qwen2.5vl:7b against a local ollama), so its description is recorded as a labelled candidate rather than extracted content, and a missing model fails the job by name. It stays listed here as history: the exemption was real until the contract could carry a model-backed route.

known_duplication: services/python-workers/document/worker_media.py (routed as media.probe) probes media headers only, while services/python-workers/media/worker_video.py extracts frames and media/worker_transcribe.py transcribes. They are complementary rather than duplicates: the probe reports container facts without decoding a sample, and the two heavier engines produce a transcript and frame events respectively. As of 2026-10-01 the transcribe engine is routed and the video engine is still awaiting a contract that can carry its parameters.
